newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Congressman Tejeda of Texas dies of cancer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Congressman Tejeda of Texas dies of cancer.

text.p: U.S. Congressman Frank Tejeda died on Thursday night after a long battle with brain cancer, a spokesman said on Friday. He was 51.
Tejeda, a Democrat and one of Texas' most powerful Hispanic office holders, died of pneumonia after chemotherapy weakened his immune system, the spokesman said.
Tejeda underwent brain surgery in October 1995 to remove a cancerous tumour, but physicians said at the time that they had not been able to get all of it.
In December, Tejeda's speech became severely impaired because of the cancer. He vowed to return to Washington this month for the start of the 105th Congress, but never made it.

Tejeda was a former U.S. Marine who was awarded a Bronze Star and a Purple Heart while serving in Vietnam. He joined the Marines after he was kicked out of school at age 17 for punching a school counsellor in the face.
After military service, he went back to school and eventually got a law degree from the University of California at Berkeley and a graduate degree from Harvard University.
He served in the Texas House of Representatives and state Senate before moving on to Congress.

Tejeda was the leader of an informal coalition that dominated politics in San Antonio's predominantly Hispanic southside. His cousin, Bexar County Commissioner Robert Tejeda said, "Our extended family in this community has lost its native son and most respected leader who has been a hero -- especially for our youth."
Funeral arrangements were still pending. Tejeda was divorced, but is survived by three children.
